mainTopic: Praise of תורה and methods of learning it: review, repetition by teachers, memory signs, and fixed times
overview: This amud is a long section of אגדה about the greatness of תורה and how to learn it well. It opens by comparing תורה to a fig tree, a hind, and a breast: it is always beloved and always gives new meaning. The story of רבי אלעזר בן פדת, so absorbed in learning that he forgot his cloak, illustrates this. Several פסוקים are then read as warnings to review and to learn little by little, like a hunter who secures each catch. A ברייתא describes how משה taught the תורה שבעל פה so that everyone heard each lesson four times. From this רבי אליעזר learns that a teacher must teach four times, while רבי עקיבא says to teach until the student has truly mastered it. The story of רבי פרידא, who taught a slow student four hundred times and then four hundred more, shows the great reward for such devotion. The amud ends with sources for using memory signs (סימנים) and for setting fixed times to learn תורה.

steps.title: תורה is like a fig tree that always has ripe fruit
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the fig-tree comparison. Just as you always find a ripe fig on the tree, you always find new meaning in דברי תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whenever a person searches the fig tree, he finds figs on it. So too with דברי תורה: whenever a person thinks deeply about them, he finds new meaning in them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a comparison that began on the previous amud: תורה is like a fig tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Figs on a tree do not ripen all at once, so there is always another ripe one to pick. In the same way, every time you return to a piece of תורה, you can find a new insight. The point is that תורה never runs dry.

keyTerms.meaning: Searches or feels around for something
Taste or meaning; here, a new insight

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The word 'בה' (in it) refers to the fig tree mentioned at the end of the previous amud.

phrases.english: Whenever a person searches it (the fig tree),
he finds figs in it.
So too, words of Torah:
whenever a person meditates upon them,
he finds meaning in them.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁאָדָם מְמַשְׁמֵשׁ בָּהּ מוֹצֵא בָּהּ תְּאֵנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the fig-tree comparison begun earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דברי תורה always give new meaning to someone who keeps thinking about them.

steps.title: תורה is like a hind, always as beloved as the first time
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני explains why the פסוק compares תורה to a hind. Just as a hind stays dear to its mate as at the first time, תורה stays dear to its learners every time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: What does the פסוק 'A loving hind and a graceful roe...' mean? Why is תורה compared to a hind? To teach you this: a hind's womb is narrow, so it is cherished by its mate every time as much as the first time. So too, דברי תורה are cherished by those who learn them every time as much as the first time.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמואל בר נחמני starts explaining a פסוק in משלי, beginning with the image of the hind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He asks why the פסוק chose a hind and answers with a natural feature of the animal: it stays as dear to its mate as at the first time. The lesson is that learning תורה should never feel old or stale. Each session can feel as fresh as the very first.

keyTerms.meaning: A loving hind (female deer), from משלי 5:19

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"A loving hind and a graceful roe, etc."?
Why were words of Torah compared to a hind?
To tell you:
just as a hind's womb is narrow,
and it is cherished by its mate
each and every time like the first time,

phrases.aramaic: אַף דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה חֲבִיבִין עַל לוֹמְדֵיהֶן
phrases.english: so too, words of Torah are cherished by those who study them
each and every time like the first time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new comparison from a new פסוק, continuing the theme of praising תורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דברי תורה remain as beloved to learners every time as they were the first time.

steps.title: תורה gives grace to those who learn it
steps.stepSummary: The next phrase of the פסוק, 'ויעלת חן', is read as a wordplay: תורה 'brings up' חן on its learners.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And a graceful roe' means that תורה bestows grace upon those who learn it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמואל בר נחמני moves to the next words of the same פסוק and explains them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'יעלת' (roe) is read as if it said 'מעלת' (brings up, bestows). So the phrase becomes a statement that תורה makes its learners pleasing and graceful in other people's eyes.

phrases.english: "And a graceful roe":
that it bestows grace upon those who study it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיַעֲלַת חֵן שֶׁמַּעֲלָת חֵן עַל לוֹמְדֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the same פסוק, moving to its next phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תורה makes those who learn it graceful and pleasing to others.

steps.title: תורה is like a breast that always gives milk
steps.stepSummary: The phrase 'דדיה ירווך בכל עת' compares תורה to a breast. A baby always finds milk there, and a learner always finds new meaning in תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Let her breasts satisfy you at all times.' Why is תורה compared to a breast? Just as a baby always finds milk whenever he nurses, so too, whenever a person thinks deeply about דברי תורה, he finds new meaning in them.
steps.whatsHappening: The explanation moves to the second half of the פסוק and uses the image of nursing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats the lesson of the fig tree from Step 1 with a new picture: the source keeps giving. The words 'בכל עת' (at all times) stress that there is never a moment when תורה has nothing left to offer.

phrases.english: "Let her breasts satisfy you at all times":
Why were words of Torah compared to a breast?
Just as this breast,
whenever the baby searches it,
he finds milk in it,
so too, words of Torah:
whenever a person meditates upon them,
he finds meaning in them.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּדֶּיהָ יְרַוֻּךָ בְכׇל עֵת לָמָּה נִמְשְׁלוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה כְּדַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same פסוק and echoes the fig-tree lesson of Step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whenever one meditates on דברי תורה, one finds new meaning.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן פדת forgot his cloak while learning
steps.stepSummary: The last phrase, 'באהבתה תשגה תמיד', is illustrated by רבי אלעזר בן פדת. He learned in the lower market of ציפורי while his cloak lay forgotten in the upper market.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Be always absorbed in her love,' as with רבי אלעזר בן פדת. They said about him that he would sit and learn תורה in the lower market of ציפורי while his cloak lay in the upper market of ציפורי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the last phrase of the פסוק and gives a real-life example of someone who lived it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תשגה' literally means to be distracted or carried away. Love of תורה should carry you away from worldly concerns. רבי אלעזר בן פדת was so absorbed in learning that he did not notice he had left his cloak far behind.

keyTerms.meaning: You will be absorbed or carried away
Tzippori, a city in the Galil

steps.confusionAlert: The printed text has 'אליעזר' in parentheses, but the correct reading is רבי אלעזר בן פדת, the well-known אמורא.

phrases.english: "Be you ravished always with her love":
as was the case with Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat.
They said of him, of Rabbi Elazar,
that he would sit and engage in Torah
in the lower marketplace of Tzippori,
and his cloak was lying
in the upper marketplace of Tzippori.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאַהֲבָתָהּ תִּשְׁגֶּה תָּמִיד כְּגוֹן רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן פְּדָת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the פסוק and illustrates its final phrase with a story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: True love of תורה makes a person absorbed in it, even forgetful of worldly things, as with רבי אלעזר בן פדת.

steps.title: A snake guarded רבי אלעזר's cloak
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from רבי יצחק בן אלעזר adds that once someone came to take the forgotten cloak and found a snake on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יצחק בן אלעזר said, once a person came to take the cloak and found a snake on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a follow-up story from a ברייתא about the forgotten cloak.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The snake was guarding the cloak. The message is that heaven protects the belongings of someone so devoted to תורה that he forgets about them himself.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: The whole פסוק 'אילת אהבים...' is read as praise of תורה: always beloved as the first time (hind), gives חן to its learners (roe), always offers new meaning (breast), and should absorb you completely (רבי אלעזר בן פדת, whose cloak heaven guarded).
steps.whyThisMatters: The story shows that devotion to תורה is not only praised but protected. That makes it a model for how a learner should relate to learning.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yitzḥak ben Elazar said:
One time a person came to take it,
and found a serpent on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר פַּעַם אַחַת בָּא אָדָם לִיטְּלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the story of רבי אלעזר בן פדת's forgotten cloak.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heaven protected the property of רבי אלעזר בן פדת while he was absorbed in תורה.

steps.title: Riders on white donkeys are traveling תלמידי חכמים
steps.stepSummary: A teaching from the school of רב ענן reads the first half of שופטים ה:י as describing תלמידי חכמים. They travel to learn, make תורה as clear as noon, and judge with complete truth.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in the school of רב ענן: What does the פסוק mean, 'Riders of white donkeys, sitters on מדין, and walkers on the way, speak'? 'Riders of donkeys' are תלמידי חכמים who travel from city to city and from country to country to learn תורה. 'White' means they make it clear as noon. 'Sitters on מדין' means they judge a true judgment with complete truth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching that reads a פסוק from שירת דבורה, phrase by phrase, as praise of תלמידי חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word of the פסוק gets a meaning through wordplay. צחורות (white) sounds like צהרים (noon), so it means making תורה bright and clear. מדין sounds like דין (judgment), so it means judging truly.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the study house of (introduces a teaching from a particular school)
Noon, the brightest time of day
Fine cloths or couches; read here as related to דין, judgment
A judgment that is true to its very core

phrases.english: It was taught in the school of Rav Anan:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"Riders of white donkeys,
those who sit on fine cloths,
and those who walk on the way, speak"?
"Riders of donkeys": these are Torah scholars,
who travel from city to city
and from province to province
to learn Torah.
"White": they make it as clear as noon.
"Those who sit on מדין":
they judge a true judgment with complete truth.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַב עָנָן: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another פסוק-based praise of תורה learners, continuing the theme of steps 2–6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The riders of white donkeys are תלמידי חכמים who travel to learn, make תורה clear, and judge truly.

steps.title: Three levels of learners: מקרא, משנה, תלמוד
steps.stepSummary: The same teaching continues with the rest of the פסוק. 'Walkers' are בעלי מקרא, 'on the way' are בעלי משנה, and 'speak' are בעלי תלמוד, whose every conversation is תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And walkers' are the masters of מקרא. 'On the way' are the masters of משנה. 'Speak' are the masters of תלמוד, because all their talk is words of תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the same teaching and reads the second half of the פסוק as three kinds of תורה learners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three phrases build from lowest to highest level: מקרא, then משנה, then תלמוד. The word שיחו (speak) fits בעלי תלמוד best, because their whole conversation is in learning.

keyTerms.meaning: Masters of תלמוד, the deep analysis of the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: This teaching praises traveling to learn, explaining clearly, judging truly, and the levels מקרא, משנה, תלמוד, with תלמוד at the top.

phrases.english: "And those who walk": these are the masters of Bible.
"On the way": these are the masters of Mishnah.
"Speak": these are the masters of Talmud,
for all their conversation is words of Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same reading of the פסוק into its second half.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק names three rising levels of learners: מקרא, משנה, and תלמוד.

steps.title: The deceitful hunter will not live long
steps.stepSummary: רב שיזבי, quoting רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, reads משלי יב:כז through wordplay: the 'רמאי' hunter will not live long. This hints at a student who keeps learning new material without holding on to what he already learned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שיזבי said in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: What does the פסוק mean, 'רמיה will not roast his catch'? It means the deceitful hunter will not live and will not have long days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching on a פסוק about a hunter and reads it as a lesson about how a person learns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word יחרוך (roast) is split into יחיה (live) and יאריך (lengthen days). A hunter who keeps chasing new animals but does not secure the ones he caught ends up with nothing. In the same way, a learner who never reviews loses his learning.

keyTerms.meaning: He will not roast (read here as 'will not live long')

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק is literally about hunting. The גמרא is using it as a picture of learning: the 'catch' is the תורה you already learned.

phrases.english: Rav Sheizvi said
in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"The slothful one will not roast his catch"?
He will not live, and he will not have long days:
phrases.notes: יחרוך is read as יחיה + יאריך

phrases.english: the deceitful hunter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁיזְבִי מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from praising learners to warning about how learning can be lost.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The deceitful hunter, a picture of the learner who does not secure what he learned, will not last.

steps.title: רב ששת: does the clever hunter really lose out?
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת pushes back with a short question: 'Will the רמאי hunter roast?' He reads רמאי as 'clever', so the clever hunter is exactly the one who does get to roast his catch.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: The רמאי hunter, will he roast? (Of course the clever hunter roasts his catch!)
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת questions the reading in the previous step. A truly רמאי (clever, crafty) hunter is the one who succeeds, not the one who fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument turns on the word רמאי. רב שיזבי read it as a failing hunter. רב ששת reads it as a crafty one, so the lesson becomes positive: the smart learner keeps his catch.

keyTerms.meaning: Will he roast? (here asked as a question)

steps.confusionAlert: This short line is a question that pushes back. It does not agree with step 9. The whole debate is about whether רמאי means 'deceitful/foolish' or 'clever'.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
Will a crafty hunter roast? (i.e., he certainly will!)

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: צַיָּיד הָרַמַּאי יַחֲרוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how step 9 understood the word רמאי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שיזבי's reading that the רמאי hunter fails
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A רמאי is crafty, and a crafty hunter is the one who succeeds in keeping and roasting his catch.

steps.title: רב דימי's parable: break each bird's wings as you catch it
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי gives a parable. A bird hunter who breaks each bird's wings one by one as he catches it keeps his birds. If he does not, they fly away. The lesson is to review each piece of learning so it stays with you.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: It is like a hunter who catches birds. If he breaks the wings of each one, one after the other, they stay. If not, they do not stay.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי explains how a 'clever hunter' succeeds, which supports רב ששת's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The clever hunter secures each catch before moving on to the next. In learning, this means reviewing each lesson right away, so it does not 'fly away' while you rush to new material.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (usually from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
Each one in turn, one by one

steps.whatToRemember: Learning is only kept if you secure it as you go. Review each piece, the way a clever hunter secures each bird, or it will slip away.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source for the value of חזרה, reviewing your learning, which is central to success in תורה.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
It is comparable to a hunter who hunts birds:
if he breaks their wings one by one,
his catch is secured;
and if not, it is not secured.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אָמַר: מָשָׁל לְצַיָּיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and supports רב ששת's reading of רמאי as 'clever' with a parable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hunter who secures each catch one by one keeps it; a learner who reviews each lesson keeps his learning.

steps.title: Learning in big bundles shrinks, gathering bit by bit grows
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא reads 'הון מהבל ימעט' through wordplay. Someone who learns his תורה in big 'bundles' (חבילות) will see it shrink, while someone who gathers it bit by bit will see it grow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said in the name of רב סחורה, who said in the name of רב הונא: What does the פסוק mean, 'Wealth from vanity will shrink, but one who gathers by hand will increase'? If a person turns his תורה into bundle after bundle, it shrinks. If not, 'one who gathers by hand will increase.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another פסוק that teaches the same lesson as רב דימי's bird parable: learn slowly and review, or you will lose what you learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הבל (vanity) is read as חבל, from חבילות, meaning bundles. Learning big loads at once without reviewing makes your knowledge fade. Gathering 'by hand', one small piece at a time, is how your knowledge actually grows.

keyTerms.meaning: Wealth (here, a person's treasure of תורה)
Vanity. Here it is read as a hint to חבילות, bundles
Bundle after bundle, meaning learning large amounts at once
Gathers by hand, meaning collects little by little

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק literally says הבל, not חבל. The דרשה works by swapping the similar-sounding letters ה and ח. Do not look for the word 'bundles' in the actual פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר (רַבָּה) אָמַר רַב סְחוֹרָה אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rabba said that Rav Seḥora said that Rav Huna said:
What is the meaning of that which is written
"Wealth gotten through vanity shall be diminished
but he who gathers little by little shall increase"
If a person makes his Torah
into bundle after bundle, it will diminish
phrases.notes: הבל is read as חבל, bundles

phrases.english: And if not
phrases.notes: Meaning, if instead he learns a little at a time and reviews.

phrases.english: "he who gathers little by little shall increase."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב דימי's lesson (step 11) with a second פסוק that teaches the same idea
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning in large bundles makes תורה shrink. Learning little by little with review makes it grow.

steps.title: The רבנן know this advice but do not follow it
steps.stepSummary: רבה remarks that the רבנן are aware of this method but still go against it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: The רבנן know this idea, and they still go against it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה adds a short, honest comment: even scholars who know they should learn slowly and review often fail to do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not missing information. It is self-discipline. Scholars are tempted to rush ahead and cover more material instead of reviewing what they already learned.

keyTerms.meaning: They go against it, they ignore it

phrases.english: Rabba said:
The Sages know this matter,
and yet they transgress it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: יָדְעִי רַבָּנַן לְהָא מִלְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A comment on how people actually live up to רב הונא's teaching
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Knowing the right way to learn is not enough. People must actually do it.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: I did it and it worked
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק testifies that he did learn little by little with review, and his learning stayed with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: I did this, and my learning lasted in my hands.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives real-life proof that רב הונא's advice works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the רבנן רבה described, he actually followed the method. His learning 'stayed in his hand', which confirms the promise of the פסוק: 'one who gathers by hand will increase.'

keyTerms.meaning: It lasted in my hands, I kept it

steps.whatToRemember: The lesson of this whole section: learn a little at a time and review it. That is how תורה stays with you.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
I did this,
and it endured in my hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with רבה's comment: here is someone who did follow the advice
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's teaching that learning bit by bit makes תורה last
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן בר יצחק's own experience

steps.title: How משה first taught the Oral Torah: Aharon and his sons
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes the order of teaching. משה learned from ה׳. Then אהרן came in and learned, then אהרן's sons came in and learned, and each group stayed seated in a set spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: What was the order of teaching משנה? משה learned straight from ה׳‎. אהרן came in, and משה taught him his lesson. אהרן moved aside and sat at משה's left. אהרן's sons came in, and משה taught them their lesson. The sons moved aside. אלעזר sat at משה's right and איתמר sat at אהרן's left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that review was built into the very first teaching of the תורה שבעל פה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each group stays in the room after its own lesson, so it hears the lesson again when the next group is taught. This is the beginning of a system where every listener hears the lesson many times.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught. This introduces a ברייתא
The order of teaching the תורה שבעל פה
From the mouth of the Almighty

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
What was the order of teaching?
Moses learned from the mouth of the Almighty.
Aaron entered,
and Moses taught him his lesson.
Aaron moved aside
and sat to the left of Moses.
His sons entered,
and Moses taught them their lesson.
His sons moved aside:
Elazar sat to the right of Moses,
and Itamar to the left of Aaron.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from advice about review to a historical model of review from the time of משה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה taught each group in turn, and each group stayed to hear the lesson again.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: אהרן always returns to משה's right
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees about the seating. He holds that אהרן always went back to sit at משה's right side.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: אהרן always returns to the right of משה.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, רבי יהודה argues with the first opinion, but only about where people sat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion gave אהרן the left side and אלעזר the right. רבי יהודה says the place of honor on the right always went back to אהרן. The order of teaching itself is not in dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: To the right, the side of honor

steps.confusionAlert: This is only an argument about seating. Both opinions agree on who learned and how many times.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Aaron always returns to the right of Moses.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לְעוֹלָם אַהֲרֹן לִימִין מֹשֶׁה חוֹזֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different opinion about the seating described in step 15
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, אהרן sits at משה's right.

steps.title: The elders and the people learn, and the first count
steps.stepSummary: The זקנים and then the whole nation come in and learn from משה. At this point אהרן has heard the lesson four times, his sons three, the זקנים two, and the people once.
steps.simpleTranslation: The זקנים came in, and משה taught them their lesson. The זקנים moved aside. The whole nation came in, and משה taught them their lesson. So אהרן had it four times, his sons three times, the זקנים two times, and the whole nation once.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes משה's round of teaching and counts how many times each group has heard the lesson so far.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since each group stayed seated, it heard every lesson that came after its own. So the earlier a group came in, the more times it heard the lesson. The groups are still uneven, and this sets up the next stage.

keyTerms.meaning: It turns out, the result is

phrases.english: The elders entered
and Moses taught them their lesson.
The elders moved aside,
the entire nation entered,
and Moses taught them their lesson.
It turns out that Aaron had it four times,
his sons three,
the elders two,
and the entire nation one.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִכְנְסוּ זְקֵנִים וְשָׁנָה לָהֶן מֹשֶׁה פִּירְקָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from רבי יהודה's side comment to the main story of the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After משה's round of teaching: אהרן heard it four times, his sons three, the זקנים two, and the people one.

steps.title: The teachers step out and teach again, so everyone hears it four times
steps.stepSummary: משה leaves and אהרן teaches. Then אהרן leaves and his sons teach. Then the sons leave and the זקנים teach. In the end, everyone has heard the lesson four times.
steps.simpleTranslation: משה left, and אהרן taught them his lesson. אהרן left, and his sons taught them their lesson. The sons left, and the זקנים taught them their lesson. So everyone ended up with four times.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the system: the teachers step out one by one, and the next group repeats the lesson. This makes everyone equal at four times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each repeat adds one hearing for everyone still in the room. The sons gain one (3→4), the זקנים gain two (2→4), and the people gain three (1→4). This fits the theme of the section: הלכה was taught from the start through careful, repeated review.
steps.whatToRemember: Even the first teaching of the תורה שבעל פה was built on repetition. Everyone, from אהרן to the simplest Jew, heard each lesson four times.

phrases.english: Moses departed
and Aaron taught them his lesson.
Aaron departed
and his sons taught them their lesson.
His sons departed,
and the elders taught them their lesson.
It turns out that everyone had it four times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the count from step 17 by evening out all the groups
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The system of teaching made sure that every Jew heard each lesson exactly four times.

steps.title: A teacher must review a lesson four times
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר learns from the ברייתא that a person must teach his student a lesson four times.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here רבי אליעזר said: A person is obligated to teach his student four times.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר takes the story of how משה taught everyone four times and turns it into a rule for all teachers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, everyone ended up hearing the lesson four times. רבי אליעזר says this was not an accident. It is the model every teacher must follow.

keyTerms.meaning: From here, meaning a rule is being drawn from the source just quoted
To teach or repeat a lesson

steps.whyThisMatters: This turns a story about the מדבר into a practical teaching obligation. It also connects back to the earlier theme of learning with review.

phrases.english: From here Rabbi Eliezer said:
phrases.notes: "Here" means the ברייתא about the order of teaching.

phrases.english: A person is obligated to teach his student
four times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general halachic rule from the conclusion of the ברייתא in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A teacher must teach his student a lesson four times.

steps.title: A קל וחומר supports the four-times rule
steps.stepSummary: A קל וחומר: if אהרן, learning from משה who learned from ה׳, needed four times, then an ordinary student learning from an ordinary teacher certainly needs four times.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is a קל וחומר: אהרן learned from משה, and משה learned from ה׳, and still it had to be done this way. An ordinary person learning from an ordinary person needs it even more.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives logical support for רבי אליעזר's rule, showing it must apply to regular people too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think the four-times system was only for the special setting of משה and אהרן. The קל וחומר flips this around. If the very best student, learning from the very best teacher, needed four reviews, then weaker students and teachers surely need at least that many.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stronger one
From the mouth of the Almighty

phrases.english: And it is an a fortiori argument:
If Aaron, who learned from the mouth of Moses,
and Moses from the mouth of the Almighty, needed it this way,
then an ordinary person learning from an ordinary person
how much more so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rule in step 19 with a logical argument.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a teacher must review four times applies to ordinary teachers and students.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from אהרן, who learned from משה, who learned from ה׳.

steps.title: Teach until the student knows it and it is organized in his mouth
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says a teacher must keep teaching until the student learns, based on ״וְלַמְּדָהּ אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״, and until it is organized in his mouth, based on ״שִׂימָהּ בְּפִיהֶם״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: How do we know a person must keep teaching his student until he learns it? Because the פסוק says, "And teach it to the children of Israel." And how do we know it must be until the material is organized in their mouths? Because the פסוק says, "Put it in their mouths."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives a different measure from רבי אליעזר. The goal is not a set number of times but real mastery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר set a number: four times. רבי עקיבא says to teach as many times as it takes until the student truly learns. He also adds a second level: the material must be so clear and organized that the student can say it over smoothly.

keyTerms.meaning: Organized and fluent in their mouths

steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא is not just repeating רבי אליעזר. רבי אליעזר gives a fixed number (four), while רבי עקיבא's standard is open-ended: keep going until the student has mastered it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
From where do we know that a person is obligated to teach his student
until he learns it?
As it says: "And teach it to the children of Israel."
And from where do we know it must be until it is organized in their mouths?
As it says: "Put it in their mouths."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִן שֶׁחַיָּיב אָדָם לִשְׁנוֹת לְתַלְמִידוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different, open-ended standard for teaching than רבי אליעזר's fixed number.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A teacher must teach until the student learns the material and has it organized and fluent.

steps.title: A teacher must show the reasons
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא continues: a teacher must show his student the reasons (פנים) behind the lesson, based on ״וְאֵלֶּה הַמִּשְׁפָּטִים אֲשֶׁר תָּשִׂים לִפְנֵיהֶם״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that a teacher must show the student the reasons? Because the פסוק says, "And these are the laws that you shall set before them."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא adds a third duty. The teacher must explain why, not just what.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לפניהם ("before them") is read as related to פנים, the inner reasons or "face" of the teaching. So the teacher must lay out the logic clearly, like a table set before someone.

keyTerms.meaning: To show him the reasons, the inner "face" of the teaching

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's three duties of a teacher: teach until the student learns, until it is fluent in his mouth, and show him the reasons.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that he is obligated to show him the reasons?
As it says: "And these are the laws
that you shall set before them."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי עקיבא's list with a third teaching duty.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A teacher must explain the reasons behind the material to his student.

steps.title: Why not have everyone learn directly from משה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the whole system was needed. Everyone could simply have learned all four times from משה himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them all learn from משה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא and challenges its setup. Why pass the lesson down through אהרן, his sons, and the זקנים instead of having משה teach everyone directly?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Learning from משה, who heard it straight from ה׳, would seem to be the best quality learning. So it looks strange that some of the teaching was handed to lesser teachers.

phrases.english: Let them all learn from Moses!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא of steps 15-18 and questions its teaching order.
steps.kashyaTarget: The order of teaching in the ברייתא, where אהרן, his sons, and the זקנים each took turns teaching.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Learning from משה directly is the best source, so there seems to be no reason to have others teach.

steps.title: To give honor to אהרן, his sons, and the זקנים
steps.stepSummary: The system was set up to give honor to אהרן and his sons, and to the זקנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was done this way in order to give honor to אהרן and his sons, and honor to the זקנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the teaching was split up on purpose so that אהרן, his sons, and the זקנים would be honored as teachers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is not about better learning but about כבוד. Letting each group teach showed the nation that these leaders were respected carriers of the תורה.
steps.whatToRemember: The four-times teaching system in the מדבר shows two things: the need for review (four times), and giving honor to the leaders who taught it.

phrases.english: In order to give honor
to Aaron and his sons,
and honor to the elders.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a reason (honor) that explains the setup
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone should have learned directly from משה, since he was the best source.
steps.terutzMaskana: The teaching was divided among others to give honor to אהרן, his sons, and the זקנים.

steps.title: Why not use a simple chain of teachers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests an easier system. משה teaches only אהרן, אהרן teaches his sons, the sons teach the זקנים, and the זקנים teach all of ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let אהרן come in and learn from משה. Then let his sons come in and learn from אהרן. Then let the זקנים come in and learn from his sons. Then let them go out and teach all of ישראל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the system again from the other direction. Why did משה have to teach everyone himself, instead of passing the תורה down a chain?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 23 the גמרא asked why everyone did not simply learn all four times from משה. Now it asks the opposite question: why did משה teach every group at all? A chain would have saved משה a lot of effort.

phrases.english: Let Aaron enter and learn from Moses,
and let his sons enter and learn from Aaron,
and let the elders enter and learn from his sons,
and let them go and teach all of Israel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining that the system gave honor to אהרן and the זקנים, the גמרא asks why משה himself needed to teach every group.
steps.kashyaTarget: The system in which משה personally taught every group
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simple chain of teachers would have honored everyone and saved משה effort, so משה's direct teaching seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Learning from משה brings special success
steps.stepSummary: משה learned straight from ה׳, so learning directly from him brings extra success.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since משה learned straight from the mouth of the Almighty, his teaching is more successful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Everyone needed to hear the תורה at least once from משה himself, because he learned it directly from ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hearing תורה from the person who received it from ה׳ helps the student absorb it in a way a chain cannot. So the system mixed two goals: honor for אהרן and the זקנים, and at least one direct lesson from משה for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: From the mouth of the Almighty
His words are helped / more successful

steps.whatToRemember: The teaching system served two goals: honor for אהרן, his sons, and the זקנים, and a direct lesson from משה for everyone, because his teaching came straight from ה׳.

phrases.english: Since Moses learned from the mouth of the Almighty,
his teaching is more successful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a reason the simpler system would be worse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A chain of teachers would work just as well and save משה effort.
steps.terutzMaskana: Hearing from משה, who learned from ה׳, brings special success, so everyone needed at least one direct lesson from him.

steps.title: Quoting רבי יהודה on where אהרן sat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה from the earlier ברייתא: אהרן always went back to sit on משה's right.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: רבי יהודה says, אהרן always returned to the right of משה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back and quotes a line from the earlier ברייתא. This is a setup line that prepares the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the חכמים say that אהרן moved to משה's left as others came in and stayed there. רבי יהודה disagrees and says אהרן always returned to the right side, the place of honor. This disagreement is needed for the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said (introduces a quote from an earlier source)

phrases.english: The Master said: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Aaron always returns to the right of Moses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא and re-quotes רבי יהודה's seating opinion (step 16) to open a new discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, אהרן always sat on משה's right.

steps.title: Whose view is the ברייתא about walking with a teacher?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that when three people walk together, the teacher is in the middle, the greater student on his right, and the lesser on his left. Does this follow only רבי יהודה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion does this ברייתא follow? Three people walking on the road: the teacher is in the middle, the greater student on his right, and the lesser student on his left. Shall we say it is רבי יהודה's view and not the חכמים'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about manners and asks which side of the argument it follows. It suggests that it matches only רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא puts the greater student on the teacher's right, just as רבי יהודה put אהרן on משה's right. The חכמים kept אהרן on the left, so it seems they hold the greater student belongs on the left. If so, the ברייתא would not fit the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom does it go?
That was taught in a ברייתא
The teacher is in the middle

phrases.english: According to whom is that which was taught:
Three who were walking on the road —
the teacher is in the middle,
and the greater one at his right, and the lesser one at his left.

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא וְלָא רַבָּנַן?
phrases.english: Shall we say it is Rabbi Yehuda and not the Sages?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי יהודה's view from step 27 to work out who the ברייתא about walking follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the walking ברייתא follow only רבי יהודה, or can it also fit the חכמים?

steps.title: It can fit the חכמים too: they did not want to trouble אהרן
steps.stepSummary: Even the חכמים agree that the greater student belongs on the right. אהרן stayed on the left only to save him the trouble of moving.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows the חכמים. אהרן stayed on the left only because moving would be a bother for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא can fit the חכמים as well. Their reason for leaving אהרן on the left was not about honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים also hold that the greater person belongs on the right. They left אהרן on the left only so he would not have to get up and move each time another group came in. So the walking ברייתא does not contradict them.
steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים never said the left side is more honorable. They kept אהרן on the left only to spare him the effort of moving.

phrases.english: You can even say it is the Sages,
because of the trouble to Aaron.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא fits both views, because the חכמים left אהרן on the left only to spare him trouble, not because the left is more honorable.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Everyone agrees that when walking, the greater student goes on the teacher's right.

steps.title: רבי פרידא's student needed four hundred lessons
steps.stepSummary: רבי פרידא had a student who learned a lesson only after hearing it four hundred times.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי פרידא had a certain student. He would teach him four hundred times, and then the student would learn it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story about how much effort a teacher must put in. This line sets up the story's main event.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the earlier idea that a teacher must keep teaching until the student knows the material. רבי פרידא did this to an extreme: four hundred times for each lesson.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי פְּרִידָא הֲוָה לֵיהּ הָהוּא תַּלְמִידָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Perida had a certain student

phrases.aramaic: דַּהֲוָה תָּנֵי לֵיהּ אַרְבַּע מְאָה זִימְנֵי וְגָמַר.
phrases.english: whom he would teach four hundred times, and he would learn.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי פְּרִידָא הֲוָה לֵיהּ הָהוּא תַּלְמִידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a story that illustrates רבי עקיבא's rule that a teacher must keep teaching until the student learns.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי פרידא taught his slow student each lesson four hundred times until he knew it.

steps.title: One day the student did not learn
steps.stepSummary: One day רבי פרידא was called away for a מצוה. He taught the usual four hundred times, but the student did not learn.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day they needed him for a מצוה matter. He taught the student, but this time the student did not learn.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: this time the usual four hundred lessons did not work. This sets up what happens next in the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something was different this day: רבי פרידא was expected somewhere else for a מצוה. Even though he taught the same number of times, the student did not succeed. The next part of the story will explain why.

phrases.english: One day they requested him for a מצוה matter.
He taught him, but he did not learn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of רבי פרידא and his student.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the day רבי פרידא was called away for a מצוה, the usual four hundred lessons did not work.

steps.title: רבי פרידא asks why today was different
steps.stepSummary: רבי פרידא asks his student why he did not learn the lesson this time, even after four hundred repetitions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי פרידא said to him: What is different now?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי פרידא is surprised that four hundred times did not work today, so he asks the student what changed. This question sets up the student's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Four hundred times always worked before, so something unusual must have happened today. The question shows the teacher wants to find the real cause instead of simply giving up on the student.

phrases.english: He said to him: Now, what is different?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the failure described in step 31.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the usual four hundred repetitions did not work this time.

steps.title: The student explains he was distracted
steps.stepSummary: The student says that once he heard his teacher was needed for a מצוה, he kept expecting him to leave and could not focus.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: From the moment they told the Master that there was a מצוה matter, my mind was distracted. Every moment I said: Now the Master will get up, now the Master will get up.
steps.whatsHappening: The student answers the question. He could not concentrate because he kept thinking his teacher was about to leave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was not the number of repetitions. It was the student's worried, distracted mind. Learning needs a calm and settled focus, and he did not have it.

keyTerms.meaning: I took my mind off it; I was distracted

phrases.english: He said to him: From that moment
when they said to the Master
there is a מצוה matter
I took my mind off the lesson
and every moment I said:

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא קָאֵי מָר, הַשְׁתָּא קָאֵי מָר.
phrases.english: Now the Master will get up, now the Master will get up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The student was distracted because he kept expecting his teacher to leave for the מצוה.

steps.title: רבי פרידא teaches another four hundred times
steps.stepSummary: רבי פרידא tells the student to focus, and then teaches him four hundred more times.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Pay attention, and I will teach you. He went back and taught him another four hundred times.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי פרידא calms the student and starts over, teaching the lesson four hundred additional times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teacher does not blame the student. He fixes the real problem, which was the student's lack of focus, and pays the full price again, even though a מצוה was waiting for him. This great devotion is what leads to the reward in the next steps.

phrases.english: He said to him: Pay attention
and I will teach you.
He went back and taught him
another four hundred times.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַב דַּעְתָּיךְ וְאַתְנֵי לִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי פרידא's response to the student's explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A devoted teacher repeats the lesson as many times as the student needs.

steps.title: A בת קול offers רבי פרידא a choice
steps.stepSummary: A בת קול asks רבי פרידא whether he wants four hundred more years of life, or for himself and his generation to merit עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A בת קול came out and said to him: Would you prefer that four hundred years be added to your life, or that you and your generation merit עולם הבא?
steps.whatsHappening: Heaven rewards רבי פרידא for his devotion by offering him a choice. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The offer of four hundred years matches the four hundred extra times he taught, so the reward is measure for measure. The choice tests what he values more: his own long life, or a spiritual reward that includes his whole generation.

phrases.english: A Divine Voice came out and said to him:
Do you prefer that they add to you
four hundred years,
or that you and your generation merit
the World-to-Come?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Heaven's reaction to רבי פרידא's devotion in step 34.

steps.title: רבי פרידא chooses עולם הבא for his generation
steps.stepSummary: רבי פרידא chooses for himself and his generation to merit עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: That I and my generation merit עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי פרידא answers the בת קול. He picks the reward that also helps his whole generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He gives up a personal benefit, long life, for a lasting reward that he shares with others. This matches the selfless spirit he showed in teaching his student.

phrases.english: He said: That I and my generation merit
the World-to-Come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the choice offered in step 35.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He chooses עולם הבא for himself and his generation.

steps.title: הקדוש ברוך הוא gives him both rewards
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא tells the angels to give רבי פרידא both rewards.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא said to them: Give him both this and that.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. Because רבי פרידא chose selflessly, he receives both long life and עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He did not choose the long life, yet he gets it as well. The message is that devotion to teaching תורה brings a very great reward.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He
this one and that one; both

steps.whatToRemember: רבי פרידא taught a slow student four hundred times, and then four hundred more. Because of this devotion he received both long life and עולם הבא for himself and his generation.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to them:
Give him this and that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story after his choice in step 36.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Selfless devotion to teaching תורה earns both long life and עולם הבא.

steps.title: רב חסדא: תורה is acquired only through memory signs
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא teaches that תורה is acquired only through סימנים, and he reads a פסוק in a new way to prove it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: תורה is acquired only with סימנים, as it says, 'Put it in their mouths.' Do not read 'שימה' (put it), but rather 'סימנה' (its sign).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new teaching about how to learn. רב חסדא says memory signs are needed to hold on to תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the story before it, this teaching is about how to succeed in learning. It uses an אל תקרי, a rereading of the word, that changes שימה to סימנה. This shows that the way to 'put' תורה into our mouths is through signs that help us remember it.

keyTerms.meaning: do not read it as, but rather as (a rereading of the word)

steps.confusionAlert: An אל תקרי does not change the words of the פסוק. It adds a second layer of meaning on top of the simple reading.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known source for using memory aids in learning, such as the סימנים found throughout the גמרא.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Torah is acquired only with signs,
as it is said: 'Put it in their mouths,'
do not read 'put it,' but rather 'its sign.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: אֵין תּוֹרָה נִקְנֵית אֶלָּא בְּסִימָנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new teaching about methods of learning, following the story about how to learn successfully.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תורה is acquired only through memory signs, learned from 'שימה בפיהם' reread as 'סימנה'.

steps.title: רבי אבהו learns the same idea from a different verse
steps.stepSummary: רב תחליפא brings רב חסדא's teaching to רבי אבהו, who says that in ארץ ישראל they learn it from 'הציבי לך ציונים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב תחליפא from the West (ארץ ישראל) heard it and went and said it before רבי אבהו. He said: You learn it from there; we learn it from here: 'Set up signposts for yourself, establish for yourself, etc.' This means: make signs for the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו agrees with the idea that סימנים are needed. However, he gives a different source for it, a פסוק in ירמיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree on the rule. They only differ on which פסוק it comes from. רבי אבהו reads 'ציונים' (signposts) as signs that a person sets up for remembering תורה.

phrases.english: Rav Tachalifa from the West heard it,
he went and said it before Rabbi Abbahu,
he said: You learn it from there,
we learn it from here:
'Set up signposts for yourself,
establish for yourself, etc.'
make signs for the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתּוּן מֵהָתָם מַתְנִיתוּ לַהּ, אֲנַן מֵהָכָא מַתְנִינַן לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different פסוק for the same rule stated in step 38.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The need for memory signs is learned from 'הציבי לך ציונים'.

steps.title: How do we know ציון means a sign?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for proof that the word ציון means a sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that this word ציון means a sign?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the basis of רבי אבהו's proof by asking what the word ציון really means. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו's whole derivation depends on ציון meaning 'sign.' So the גמרא asks for a source that shows this meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: how is it implied? how do we know?

phrases.english: And from where is it implied that this 'tziyun'
is a term meaning 'sign'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּהַאי צִיּוּן לִישָּׁנָא דְסִימָנָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the key word in רבי אבהו's פסוק from step 39.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that ציון means a sign.

steps.title: Proof from the marker set beside a human bone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from a פסוק in יחזקאל that ציון means a sign: a marker is placed beside a human bone.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And he sees a human bone, and he builds a ציון beside it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that clearly uses ציון to mean a marker or sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In יחזקאל, a ציון is set up next to a bone to warn people about טומאה at that spot. Since there ציון clearly means a sign, it means a sign in ירמיה as well, and רבי אבהו's proof works.
steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא and רבי אבהו both teach that תורה must be learned with memory signs. They only differ on the source פסוק, and the word ציון is proven to mean 'sign.'

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And he sees a human bone
and builds a sign beside it.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״וְרָאָה עֶצֶם אָדָם וּבָנָה אֶצְלוֹ צִיּוּן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 40.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In יחזקאל, ציון is a marker set beside a bone, so the word means a sign.

steps.title: A third source for signs from משלי
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר brings a פסוק from משלי and reads 'ומודע לבינה' as a command to make signs that help you know the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said: We learn it from here: "Say to wisdom, you are my sister, and call understanding your kinswoman (מודע)". This means: make signs (מודעים) for the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives another source for the idea that you need signs to remember תורה. This one comes from a פסוק in משלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מודע' in the פסוק simply means a relative or close friend. רבי אליעזר hears in it the root 'ידע', to know, and reads it as 'מודעים', things that make you know. So the פסוק becomes an instruction to create signs that help your understanding of תורה stay with you.

keyTerms.meaning: A relative or close friend (in the plain reading of the פסוק)
Things that make you know, meaning signs or memory aids

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said: from here:
phrases.notes: Here comes a third source, alongside רב חסדא's פסוק and the 'הציבי לך ציונים' from ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: "Say to wisdom, you are my sister,
phrases.notes: משלי ז:ד. Treat wisdom as something as close to you as family.

phrases.english: and call understanding your kinswoman (moda)"
make signs (moda'im) for the Torah.
phrases.notes: The דרשה: 'מודע' is read as 'מודעים', things that make you know.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another פסוק as a source for רב חסדא's rule about סימנים, next to רבי אבהו's 'הציבי לך ציונים' that was just proven in step 41.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Make signs and memory aids for תורה, learned from 'ומודע לבינה תקרא'.

steps.title: רבא reads the same word as fixed times for learning
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads the same word as 'מועדים', set times, and so learns a different lesson: set fixed times for learning תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: make set times (מועדים) for the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא reads the same פסוק in a different way. For him, it teaches that a person must set fixed times for learning תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא changes one letter in his reading: not 'מודעים' (signs) but 'מועדים' (appointed times). So for him the פסוק is not about memory tricks. It is about keeping a steady, regular schedule of learning, and that also keeps the תורה with you.
steps.whatToRemember: Two ways to hold on to תורה come out of 'ומודע לבינה תקרא'. רבי אליעזר says to make signs (מודעים), and רבא says to set fixed times (מועדים).
steps.confusionAlert: 'מודעים' and 'מועדים' look and sound almost the same, but they mean different things. רבי אליעזר means signs that help you know. רבא means set times on a schedule.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבא's reading is a well-known source for the practice of setting fixed times for learning תורה.

phrases.english: Rava said:
phrases.notes: Gives a different reading of the same פסוק.

phrases.english: Set appointed times (mo'adim) for the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the same פסוק that רבי אליעזר used, but takes a different lesson from it: set times instead of signs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Set fixed times for learning תורה, learned from reading 'מודע' as 'מועד'.
